January 30, 1933.
Dear Debby
This aeries two of my shot gun correspondence being broadcast
from somewhere on the storm tossed so called Pacific Ocean. We sailed from
Victoria at five thirty Saturday afternoon, and after passing through the
straits headed out across the Paoifio. We immediately ran into what the Cap-
tain calls " a bit of nasty weather " which has put most of the few passengers
in their respective staterooms. Saturday night there were only three men who
showed up for dinner besides Groeger and meself. Groeger is an old sailing
ship captain so the thick weather bothers him not at all. So far it has not
effected me and I am hoping that I will turn out to be a good sailor - I have
really never been in rough weather before as my very limited experience has
all been in fair weather. The ship is rolling and plunging so that it is ex-
remely hard to get around. Outaide the oold spray is flying the whole length
of the ship and the rigging is loe covered. There are no games on deok and
no steamer chairs. The few passengers who venture out of their rooms sit
around the open fires in the "tap room" and work on their "seotch and Soda".
Yesterday, Sunday, Groeger and I called on the Captain and made arrangements
for Groeger to have access to the bridge and chart room so that he can make
the weather obversations which he was instructed to secure. The Captain is an
Englishman who has sailed all over the World during his thirty years at sea,
and he seems to enjoy swapping yarns with Groeger and giving information on
flying conditions. He is very much ammused at the idea of ever flying across
the Pacific and of course knows nothing whatever about airtransportation or
its limitations. Lest night we had a Movie, Careless Age, featuring Douglas
Fairbanke and Loreta Young. It was an old "talkie" with no talking. The girls
• wore dresses which came just to the lees and looked awfully funny. After each
reel a sign came on "ONE MOMENT PLEASE" and the Chink who was the operator
would put on the next reel. All the crew except the officers are Chinese and
none of them can underatand English. My stateroom steward looks like & Guinea
Pig and so I call him "G P". He gives me a lot of service as he has no one else
to look after. This morning Groeger and I took "shots" for Typhold and Friday
